summary: The candidate correctly rejects known equivalent spellings of the same local or Hub checkpoint from using GLM5's bundled NextN head as EAGLE3. This is a valid partial safety fix, not a semantic or performance fix for the original issue.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before collection on recorded base; the new validator was absent.
Exact candidate regression and existing GLM5 hidden-state capture tests: 9 passed and 3 subtests passed.

tests.command: Direct adversarial calls to _validate_native_mtp_algorithm for local aliases and Hub revisions
tests.what_was_measured: Existing path aliases and equivalent Hub revisions were rejected; distinct revisions/repositories were allowed.

tests.command: ROCm tensor shape probe for H=4096, hc_mult=4 on cuda
tests.what_was_measured: One mHC capture was width 16384 and three concatenated captures width 49152, both incompatible with an H-wide 4096 input.

gpu_execution.evidence: A shape-only torch tensor probe ran on one AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950. No GLM5 model or fused kernel executed.

remaining_counterexamples: Bundled NEXTN/EAGLE acceptance and throughput remain unverified; the reported acceptance near 1.0 is unresolved.
A distinct EAGLE3 draft remains allowed without evidence of GLM5 architecture compatibility or successful execution.
The patch blocks the known bundled-head EAGLE3 configuration but does not correct EAGLE3/mHC hidden-state semantics.
remaining_limitations: The environment has one AMD MI355X gfx950 with ROCm 7.2, not 4x NVIDIA H20 TP=4.
No full server, fused CUDA kernel, model acceptance, or throughput run was performed.
No native files changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
